The flanking rule classifies the CHARACTER next to a delimiter run, not the byte. An em dash is punctuation, so *—*bravo. stays literal, and so does ~~—~~bravo.

A pound sign is punctuation under CommonMark's definition too, so *£*bravo. stays literal: that is spec example 354.

A letter is a word character in every script, so аб really is emphasis.

The line below has a NO-BREAK SPACE (U+00A0) on each side of the "a". A no-break space is Unicode whitespace, so the run before it cannot open emphasis, and it is not ASCII whitespace, so the line is not a list either:

* a *
